input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: Deepen flagship 4 (changepoint-detector): a labelled set to turn agreement tiers into a detection rate
errors: First port check differed from the published scores by 0.33 until I applied TCPDBench summarize.py's clean_cps (drop indexes <1 or >n-2); fixed and re-checked to 2.2e-16.
TCPDBench abed_results 'result' field is sometimes a dict, sometimes a Python-repr string; handled both.

doc_friction.issue: 'take the top Deepen row of allocate.py' sent me to wall-framing-takeoff (267 commits in 7 days, every listed item needing real inputs no run has; recent ROADMAP entries are one-flag CLI validation fixes). The allocator could down-rank a flagship whose next: is all 'wanted: real X' and whose recent commits are saturated.
check_post_frontmatter.py and check_post_links.py take no file argument (they scan docs/posts); passing a path errors. Minor, cost one call.

deviations.why: Top flagship (wall-framing-takeoff) is saturated and every open item needs real inputs not available; flagship 4's ask (a labelled set) was satisfiable today from a public MIT benchmark.
deviations.result: Landed a benchmark with a verified metric port, a measured tier hit rate in the product, and the first outside evidence that the default level model loses to 'no change'.

notes: TCPD data fetched at run time (not committed: per-series GPL/CC BY-SA terms). Metric port reproduces 121 published default runs to 2.2e-16. No defaults changed: split-half support threshold did not reliably beat 'no change'. No separate docs/reports agent doc: the README section and the flagship next: carry everything the next run needs.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: porting and validating a benchmark metric against published scores, writing the eval and the write-ups, for a statistician

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
